A1.justification: Both PDFs describe W-Bench and VINE. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermarking evaluations, component ablations, frequency analyses, and appendix experiments on resolution scaling and editing quality.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds real-image inversion examples, edited-watermark frequency analyses, and MAGE+ video-generation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain VINE's architecture, losses, blurring surrogates, staged training, fine-tuning, and resolution scaling. The new detection discussion does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix G.4 adds evaluation on CATER-GEN-v2 using MAGE+ text-image-to-video generation, extending the image-only SVD scenario with text conditioning and another dataset. Existing training and evaluation coverage remains.

E2.justification: The eleven quantitative baselines are unchanged and reused for MAGE+. New Figure 6 separately examines Tree Ring, RingID, and Gaussian Shading with inversion, but does not compare them against VINE or include them in W-Bench.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 50-step inversion for the real-image examples and a MAGE+ protocol using 1,000 input images, 10-frame videos, and detection on frames 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a feasibility case study of applying in-generation watermarks to real images through inversion. Figure 8 adds diagnostics of actual watermark spectra after four editing processes, extending v1's unedited-spectrum analysis. Existing component ablations and resolution-scaling analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly documents watermark detection as a hypothesis test with binomial matching-bit counts and analytic FPR/TPR calculations. This adds statistical reporting, without establishing additional runs or adding seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports MAGE+ average TPR@0.1%FPR of 90.29% for VINE-Base, 91.35% for VINE-Robust, and 89.34% for StegaStamp. These are results under new conditions, not gains over the retained SVD results. Figures 6 and 8 add qualitative findings; original quantitative tables and benchmark plots retain their results.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds Bernoulli/binomial assumptions, detection hypotheses, probability-tail expressions, and a numerical example explaining the limitations of bit accuracy. Equation 4 uses an inclusive threshold, whereas Equations 5–6 use a strict threshold. Existing mathematical content is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same W-Bench scope, frequency-based surrogate insight, SDXL-Turbo adaptation, and claims about VINE's quality and robustness. Added appendix evidence does not redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 contextualizes EditGuard's performance through its tamper-localization purpose and mild training degradation. Appendix B clarifies that the observed frequency-pattern correlation emerged after training and acknowledges difficulty isolating frequency-band effects. Appendix G.1 expands the rationale for editing coverage; existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents DDIM/DPM inversion and its step count for the new examples, plus MAGE+ video length and frame-selection details. Training hyperparameters, hardware, iteration counts, inference costs, and code-access information are retained despite appendix renumbering.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references, including the MAGE+ source, and expands discussion of applying in-generation watermarking to real images. It also clarifies EditGuard's intended role. The principal positioning of W-Bench and VINE remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include localized wording edits, conference-header and acknowledgment updates, expanded appendix explanations, and insertion of the statistical-test appendix and editing-selection subsection.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6 and 8 and the MAGE+ results table. The retained frequency visualization gains a formula label and expanded caption, while v1 Figure 15 becomes Figure 17 with additional 40×40 magnified image and residual columns. Other figures are principally retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens two explanations with direct evidence: edited-watermark spectra supplement v1's unedited spectra, and inversion examples support the exclusion of in-generation methods. MAGE+ modestly broadens validation, while enlarged residual views improve inspection. These incremental benefits outweigh the localized threshold inconsistency introduced in Appendix C; the main method and original results remain unchanged.
